title: Martin Scorsese Says His ‘Cleopatra’ Movie With Angelina Jolie Was ‘Ruined’ by Seth Rogen and the Sony Hack: ‘It Was Gonna Be Really Wild’
description:
Martin Scorsese‘s “Cleopatra” never came to fruition, and he says the Angelina Jolie-starrer was nixed because of Seth Rogen and the Sony hack.

	F
body:
Martin Scorsese‘s “Cleopatra” never came to fruition, and he says the Angelina Jolie-starrer was nixed because of Seth Rogen and the Sony hack.

	For those who need a refresher, Sony emails were hacked in November 2014 by a group that hoped the Seth Rogen comedy “The Interview,” which was about a fictional assassination attempt of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, would not be released by Sony.


	According to Scorsese, this caused some aftereffects in the industry, which he described in the first episode of the Tribeca original series “Crafty.”
	

	“We were gonna do Cleopatra at one point, and then they made fun of [Kim Jong Un], and he got mad and blew up everybody at Columbia,” Scorsese said. “Seth Rogen, right? And then he got mad, and [it] ruined Cleopatra.”

	Though Rogen wasn’t directly responsible for the project being canceled, the resulting hack exposed thousands of emails, including ones from producer Scott Rudin to Sony’s Amy Pascal calling Jolie “a minimally talented spoiled brat.” 

	“We were gonna do it,” Scorsese also said. “Angelina Jolie. We were going. She was gonna be Cleopatra VII. It was gonna be really wild.”

	The film was set to be written by screenwriter Eric Roth, who wrote Scorsese’s 2023 film “Killers of the Flower Moon.”

	Watch the episode of “Crafty” below.

schema.headline: Martin Scorsese Says His ‘Cleopatra’ Movie With Angelina Jolie Was ‘Ruined’ by Seth Rogen and the Sony Hack: ‘It Was Gonna Be Really Wild’

title: Bill Maher Fires Back at Trump by Comparing Him to Taylor Swift
description:
Bill Maher learned that when it comes to Donald Trump, no good deed goes unpunished.

	On last week’s episode of “Real Time with Bill Maher,” the p
body:
Bill Maher learned that when it comes to Donald Trump, no good deed goes unpunished.

	On last week’s episode of “Real Time with Bill Maher,” the political pundit defended his recent White House dinner with the president, exclaiming, “You know what? Fuck you. I like these dinners,” before conducting an embarrassingly chummy interview with Trump’s former press secretary, Karoline Leavitt. Despite all his brown-nosing, Trump lashed out at Maher in a 1,300-word Truth Social tirade Sunday night, calling the comic a “complete and total loser” and “major POTHEAD” who “looked like hell” during their dinner this month, where they were joined by ESPN pundit Stephen A. Smith and former rapper Kid Rock. Trump also claimed that Maher had begged him for years to go on his HBO show, but he “will never watch it again, because it is nothing more than FAKE NEWS that America, and the World, is unfortunately subjected to.”
	

	Well, Maher took the stage of “Real Time” Friday night and, before welcoming Ted Cruz and the aforementioned Kid Rock as guests, wasted no time addressing that incredibly long Trump rant.

	“Did you see the 1,300-word [Truth Social post] he sent out? Longest ever! Kind of a flex,” offered Maher during his monologue. “I tell ya, dining at the White House is the opposite of the Cheesecake Factory — after you leave, they review you!”

	“He went off on me like Kelly Clarkson in a toy store,” he continued. “Eating with Trump is like dating Taylor Swift: It’s a lot of laughs at the time, but later on, they’re tearing you a new asshole.”
	

	Maher wasn’t finished: “Look, I don’t want it to be this way. The whole point of having these dinners was talk, disagree but listen — which he does, in person — but don’t hate each other, I go back to my job here and the heartaches begin. I’m not going to refute everything, but I do have to address a few of the allegations.”

	The comic then read from a printout of Trump’s 1,300-word Truth Social post: “It begins: ‘Let’s talk about the complete and total loser Bill Maher’ — you got me there. I’ll own that,” he admitted, adding, “This is what pisses me off — he doesn’t even notice what I actually said.” Maher refuted Trump’s claim that Maher didn’t think it would be a good idea to disarm Iran by showing a clip of him stating the exact opposite on his show. Then, as to Trump’s claim that Maher “calls him incessantly,” he alleged, “I’ve never called you. You call me! I’d be afraid to call you — you’re the president, I think you’re too busy (well, plainly not).”

	Maher then said it was ridiculous that Trump claimed he “invited himself to the White House,” and that he had “a severely bruised eye and nose area,” by running pictures of him from that day without them.

	I think it’s safe to say these two won’t be breaking bread anytime soon.

schema.headline: Bill Maher Fires Back at Trump by Comparing Him to Taylor Swift

title: Bill Maher Fact-Checks Kid Rock After He Compares Abdul El-Sayed to 9/11 Hijackers on ‘Real Time’
description: Bill Maher opened his new episode of “Real Time” Friday night by addressing Trump’s 1,300-word social media tirade against him following their Whit
body:
Bill Maher opened his new episode of “Real Time” Friday night by addressing Trump’s 1,300-word social media tirade against him following their White House dinner earlier this month, with the comic comparing the president to Taylor Swift.

	Following a sit-down interview with Republican Senator Ted Cruz, who was busy hawking his new book on Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas, Maher welcomed his panel — Jim VandeHei, the co-founder and CEO of Axios, and Kid Rock, a singer who once rapped, “Young ladies, young ladies, I like ‘em underage, see / Some say that’s statutory — but I say it’s mandatory.”
	

	Kid Rock was present at that Oct. 15 White House dinner with Trump, Maher and ESPN pundit Stephen A Smith, and appeared to defend Maher against Trump’s series of claims in his record-breaking Truth Social post.

	“He said I was drunk. I was not drunk,” claimed Maher, to which Kid Rock replied, “You were pretty high.” “We had a good time — and it was four hours, right?” asked Maher. “We had a good time,” offered Kid Rock, adding, “I had to leave early, but yes, it was… Was he talking about dinner or the whole thing?”

	After their exchange over the White House dinner, Maher brought up how former president Obama campaigned for Abdul El-Sayed, a Democratic candidate for Senate in Michigan, who is Muslim. Maher said, “As far as this issue goes about Islam in America and candidates who are Muslim, the left is naïve and the right is hysterical.” He then quoted Trump, who said of El-Sayed, “If Abdul and the Democrats win, they will open the floodgates and welcome hordes of jihadists to our shores, creating a nightmare of violence and terror until you cannot even have a Christmas.”
	

	“You don’t really believe that,” Maher questioned Kid Rock, who grew up on a sprawling estate in the suburbs of Michigan. Kid Rock subsequently compared El -Sayed to the 9/11 hijackers, saying, “People talk about assimilation too all the time, right? This man very much has assimilated — good education, well-spoken, even a good-looking guy — [but] you know who else assimilated very well? Those pieces of shit that flew those planes into our World Trade Centers. The Fort Hood shooter. This has happened all over the world, so it scares the hell out of me, this Islamic extremism. I don’t know, is he a wolf in sheep’s clothing, or is he just a wolf in a wolf’s clothing?”

	Maher replied, “Not that it matters so much, but the 9/11 hijackers weren’t here assimilated. They were from Saudi Arabia.”

	“The ones who flew the planes were from Saudi Arabia? No,” Kid Rock shot back.

	In fact, 15 of the 19 9/11 hijackers were from Saudi Arabia, two were from the United Arab Emirates, one was from Egypt and one was from Lebanon, and the first hijackers to arrive in the U.S. came in January of 2000, so they weren’t “assimilated very well,” as the man formerly known as Robert James Ritchie so boldly claimed.

schema.headline: Bill Maher Fact-Checks Kid Rock After He Compares Abdul El-Sayed to 9/11 Hijackers on ‘Real Time’

title: Marvin R. Shanken, Longtime Publisher and Editor of Wine Spectator, Dies at 83
description: Marvin R. Shanken, the longtime editor and publisher of Wine Spectator magazine who was instrumental in elevating the profile of American wine busi
body:
Marvin R. Shanken, the longtime editor and publisher of Wine Spectator magazine who was instrumental in elevating the profile of American wine business, died Thursday in Manhattan. He was 83. 

	Shanken started his career in 1972 when he bought a small industry newsletter named Impact, which became a key resource for the wine and spirits industries. He purchased the struggling Wine Spectator newspaper in 1979, which he turned into a glossy magazine with more than 100,000 subscribers. 
	

	Wine Spectator became a key educational tool to help consumers become more familiar with the beverage, and contributed significantly to raising the status of the Napa Valley wine region. Wine Spectator articles utilized the 100 point wine rating system, which made buying fine bottles much more approachable for the general audience.

	Shanken also founded the magazine Cigar Aficionado and purchased Food Arts and Malt Advocate, which was renamed Whisky Advocate. Other publications he founded through his M. Shanken Communications include Market Watch and Shanken News Daily.   

	“He helped educate millions of Americans on the joys and virtues of wine, and tirelessly encouraged and pushed winemakers to produce the best for their customers,” Wine Spectator wrote in its obituary. 

	Among his many milestones were establishing Wine Spectator’s Restaurant Awards program, taking over the long-running Wine Experience weekend to bring producers together with consumers and creating the Wine Spectator Scholarship Foundation. 

	“It was an extremely influential publication that, along with Robert Parker, actually affected the way wine was made. Wine Spectator could make wineries halfway around the world change the way they made wine,” W. Blake Gray of the website Wine-Searcher told the New York Times. 
	

	Born in New Haven, Connecticut, Shanken studied business at the U. of Miami, then received an MBA from American U. in Washington. 

	He started off working in investment banking on Wall Street, during which time he was sent to California to help finance a vineyard purchase. This led to him developing a strong interest in wine and the industry. He pivoted his career to running the Impact newsletter, encouraged by its reception from alcoholic beverage wholesalers. At the time, there was very little substantial reporting on the wine business. 

	After he bought the struggling Wine Spectator newspaper, he relocated the offices from San Diego to San Francisco and became editor. The magazine expanded to cover travel, cooking, restaurants and collecting, and recently celebrated its 50th anniversary.  

	Shanken is survived by his wife, Hazel Rudy, daughters Jessica, Allison and Samantha, four grandchildren and two sisters.

schema.headline: Marvin R. Shanken, Longtime Publisher and Editor of Wine Spectator, Dies at 83

title: Two Arrested in Murder of ‘SNL’ Writer’s Sister
description: Two suspects have been arrested in connection with the murder of Christina Downer, “Saturday Night Live” writer Jimmy Fowlie’s sister, according to
body:
Two suspects have been arrested in connection with the murder of Christina Downer, “Saturday Night Live” writer Jimmy Fowlie’s sister, according to the Los Angeles Police Department.

	Delorean Bijon Brandon, 41, Downer’s boyfriend, and Kaylee Nicole Markowski, 34, were arrested Thursday in Highland Park and Tarzana, respectively. Detectives believe Brandon and Markowski were responsible for Downer’s murder and then disposed of her body and concealed the crime.
	

	Downer was reported missing after a welfare check on Dec. 18, 2025, and Brandon claimed she had moved out and left behind her car and dog. 

	LAPD said law enforcement officials continued to investigate Downer’s disappearance after her cell phone washed ashore on the beach in Santa Monica. Authorities were led to search an Airbnb property in Joshua Tree, located in the high desert several hours from Los Angeles, in connection with her disappearance and conducted an extensive search with K-9 units and the San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department.

	Downer is “no longer alive,” her brother said on April 29.

	“Our prayers for her to be found safely have transformed into prayers for the truth to be revealed and for those responsible to be held accountable,” Fowlie’s post from April 29 read. “We have reason to believe that in the weeks before she went missing, her phone and social media were compromised. The individual(s) in possession of her phone used it to hide the fact she was gone, to ask for money and to create a false narrative that she was going ‘off the grid.’”

schema.headline: Two Arrested in Murder of ‘SNL’ Writer’s Sister

title: ‘Obsession’ Director Curry Barker Pitched Nathan Fielder a Collaboration After Watching ‘You Can See Everything’: ‘I Put It Out in the Water’
description: “Obsession” director Curry Barker is not only a fan of “You Can See Everything,” but he’s already reached out to Nathan Fielder about working toget
body:
“Obsession” director Curry Barker is not only a fan of “You Can See Everything,” but he’s already reached out to Nathan Fielder about working together.

	“I thought it was freakin’ insane and awesome,” Barker told Variety Thursday night at the Time100 Next Gala at Pier59 Studios . “I didn’t know much about [Elizabeth Holmes’] story going into it. I feel like I missed certain tiny things, but it was three hours long and I wished it was longer. That’s rare, you know?”
	

	When asked about potentially collaborating with Fielder, the “Obsession” director revealed he’s already floated the idea to him: “I told him that. I said, ‘Hey!’ … I just put it out in the water.”

	“You Can See Everything” blurs the line between narrative and documentary storytelling and, as Variety’s chief awards editor Clayton Davis puts it, has “turned the movie landscape topsy-turvy.” Much like Barker’s “Obsession,” the film has left the industry re-examining what kinds of movies resonate with Gen Z audiences — and, more importantly, what drives them out to the theaters.

	“It felt new, fresh, different,” Barker said of “You Can See Everything.” “You almost can’t even call it a documentary, but it totally is. I’m just a huge fan of what [Fielder] is doing.”

	Barker should have plenty more chances to cross paths with Fielder on the awards circuit, as both their films continue to earn recognition alongside some of the year’s most acclaimed films.

	“The events are really cool,” Barker said. “I did the Academy Gala and I was just blown away. I mean, every direction you look is someone that you’ve seen your entire life on social media, and you’re like, ‘Holy cow, this person’s here. This person’s here.’ That was a crazy experience.”
	

	But one celebrity encounter in particular left Barker starstruck: Emma Watson.

	“I was a huge ‘Harry Potter’ fan growing up, and I saw Emma Watson and I froze,” Barker recalled. “It’s so weird, I’m meeting all of these people that I really look up to, but there’s something different about when it’s someone from your childhood that really means a lot. That changes where you’re like, ‘Oh, woah.’ I was totally weird to her. I was trying to play it cool. But I did not play it cool.”

	Barker was honored alongside Raye, Druski, Paapa Essiedu and several other Hollywood rising stars at Time100 Next. The night kicked off with an intimate performance from Raye, who performed a jazzy rendition of “Cry Me a River” and “Happier Times Ahead.” Himesh Patel, Alex Warren and several other nominees made toasts throughout the night, but Ashley Padilla of “Saturday Night Live” fame got the biggest reaction from the crowd.“It’s hard to give a toast when you believe you should not be here,” the comedian quipped. “I was going to say something like the children when they asked me who or what gives me hope for the future. But I realized I don’t know any. I know my niece and nephew. and one of them called me a bitch last week. I’m not gonna say which… my niece! My nephew’s an angel. But I’m not gonna hang all my hope on those guys!”Next up for Barker is “Anything But Ghosts,” set for release on May 7, 2027. Seth Rogen, who penned Barker’s Time100 Next profile, already saw the film — and claims that Barker’s sophomore feature is “even better” than “Obsession.”

	“I’ve seen Curry’s next film, ‘Anything But Ghosts’ — and for those of you who, like me, are uncomfortable with this amount of talent in a person so young, I have bad news … it’s even better,” Rogen wrote. “And, to add insult to injury, he’s just as good an actor as he is a director.”

schema.headline: ‘Obsession’ Director Curry Barker Pitched Nathan Fielder a Collaboration After Watching ‘You Can See Everything’: ‘I Put It Out in the Water’

title: Selma Blair Apologizes for Plane Incident: ‘I Am So Sorry’
description: Selma Blair issued a video apology on Friday for the Oct. 11 incident in which she allegedly injured a flight attendant and kicked a nurse after be
body:
Selma Blair issued a video apology on Friday for the Oct. 11 incident in which she allegedly injured a flight attendant and kicked a nurse after being removed from a plane at John F. Kennedy International Airport.

	Blair, 54, is facing two state charges of 2nd-degree assault for the alleged attacks on the nurse and a Port Authority officer. 

	In a video posted to Instagram, the “Cruel Intentions” and “Legally Blonde” actress said she had been advised by her attorneys not to say much about the case.
	

	“What I can tell you, though, is very simple, and the truest thing I know about myself, and that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life,” she said. “And so to the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, I frightened, alarmed: I am so sorry.”

	Blair’s reps have previously blamed a “medical emergency” for the episode aboard the flight from L.A. to New York.

	Blair was released from custody on $20,000 bail the following day. Blair’s attorney, Shawn Barnes, said in court that she had gotten on the flight after missing several doses of a drug that controls neurological symptoms. She also fell and hit her head during the flight.

	“These factors, your honor, coupled with the altitude, resulted in a state of severe confusion and disorientation,” Barnes said. “Ms. Blair did not get on that plane intending for any of this.”

	Blair is due back in court in Queens on Jan. 19.

schema.headline: Selma Blair Apologizes for Plane Incident: ‘I Am So Sorry’

title: Cate Blanchett-Backed Group and Collection of Hollywood Stars File Brief in New York Times-OpenAI Lawsuit: Hollywood Has ‘Proven Infrastructure’ to License Content
description: The Human Consent Foundation, the Cate Blanchett-backed nonprofit trying to protect the likenesses of individuals from unauthorized scraping by AI
body:
The Human Consent Foundation, the Cate Blanchett-backed nonprofit trying to protect the likenesses of individuals from unauthorized scraping by AI models, and a legion of Hollywood companies have filed an amicus brief in the New York Times‘ lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming the tech companies’ position that it could not reasonably clear the rights for content “mischaracterizations” in light of an active licensing market. 
	

	The group’s 31-page brief was filed in the Southern District of New York late Friday, and the group was joined by CAA, the Music Artists Coalition, the National Association of Voice Actors, Writer, Inc, and the Creative Coalition on AI. The brief featured an appendix with a suite of Hollywood stars supportive of the cause, including Anne Hathaway, Emma Thompson, Dan Levy, Ron Howard, Madonna, Olivia Wilde and more.


	“Defendants have argued that licensing creative works for AI training is cost-prohibitive,” the brief read. “Defendants also claim there is no settled means of valuing training data. The facts demonstrate otherwise. The creative industries already have in place a proven infrastructure and workflows to clear rights for dispersed works at scale and cost-effectively.”

	In a statement, HCF co-founder and CEO Nikki Hexum said the filing was intended to show the court “how the creative industry actually works and acknowledge the solutions that have been built and are continuing to develop for this new digital era.”

	“Our goal is to ensure that as the market for AI data licensing grows, the humans who create the value in that market are protected and have a meaningful choice,” Hexum added. “We are not starting from scratch. There is already a functioning market and infrastructure for licensing creative work. We just need to ensure that new AI technology respects those boundaries and choices, including the choice not to participate.”
	

	The Human Consent Foundation was founded as RSL Media in May by Hexum and Blanchett, launching a registry in June where people could log what permissions they gave AI models to scrape their likenesses. The HCF is also backed by Steven Soderbergh, and he and Blanchett offered statements in the brief declaring that the principle of permission should not change in the AI era.

	“I’ve been working in film and theater for over 30 years, and in that time, the principle has never changed,” Blanchett said in the brief. “If someone wants to use my face, my voice or my image, they ask me first. There is a contract. There is a conversation. This isn’t a new idea or a complicated legal framework, it is simply how we treat each other in this industry. Consent isn’t a barrier to creativity, it is the foundation of it.”

	Other celebrity signatories include Ariana DeBose, Bette Midler, Christian Vesper, Christine Vachon, Helen Mirren, Dave Eggers, Francesca Amfitheatrof, Greg Berlanti, Julia Roberts, Melody Walker, Nina Gregory, Paul Feig, Ram Bergman, Rian Johnson, Richard Louderback, Robert De Niro, Rosario Dawson, Scarlett Johansson, Vince Gilligan and the Stan Lee Foundation.

	An OpenAI spokesperson pointed Variety to a blog post published on Friday featuring briefs from several groups — including the U.S. government, as of last month — in support of the tech giant’s position that its scraping was protected by the “fair use” doctrine, which gives people the right to use copyrighted work without the rights holder’s permission in select cases.

	“Experts and leaders across a wide range of fields have recognized that fair use is a win-win that benefits everyone, and have shared their perspectives with the Court in filing briefs in support of fair use,” the post read.

	Microsoft did not respond to an immediate request for comment.

	The amicus brief came a day after SAG-AFTRA, the Writers Guild of America and the American Federation of Musicians filed their own brief against OpenAI and Microsoft, urging the court that the tech companies’ claim that their actions constituted fair use “would render moot the terms the unions and the industry agreed to at the bargaining table.”

	“It would harm not just the copyright owners, but the people who create the work,” their Thursday brief read.
	

	The New York Times filed its lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, one of the startup’s chief backers, in December 2023, alleging the ChatGPT founder violated the publisher’s copyright by scraping thousands of news articles without permission. The Times filed for summary judgment in the case last month.

schema.headline: Cate Blanchett-Backed Group and Collection of Hollywood Stars File Brief in New York Times-OpenAI Lawsuit: Hollywood Has ‘Proven Infrastructure’ to License Content

title: ‘Kelly Clarkson Show,’ ‘General Hospital,’ ‘Beyond the Gates’ Lead Daytime Emmys 2026 Winners
description: “The Kelly Clarkson Show” went out with a bang. The daytime talk show won five awards at the 53rd Daytime Emmys on Friday, including the top daytim
body:
“The Kelly Clarkson Show” went out with a bang. The daytime talk show won five awards at the 53rd Daytime Emmys on Friday, including the top daytime talk prize, the most of any program. Meanwhile, ABC’s “General Hospital” scored the top daytime drama prize (for the sixth consecutive year), winning four overall — tied with CBS’ newcomer “Beyond the Gates,” which also won four in its first year of eligibility.

	This year’s Daytime Emmys came as a bittersweet moment for now-canceled talk shows “The Kelly Clarkson Show” and “Sherri.” “Sherri” host Sherri Shepherd won for daytime talk host, while “Kelly Clarkson” (besides best daytime talk) also won for directing for a daytime studio non-fiction series, hairstyling/makeup, art direction / set decoration / scenic design and sound mixing/editing. Because of the eligibility window, both shows will still be eligible for Daytime Emmys next year, as they produced original episodes in 2026.
	

	Among soaps, “Beyond the Gates” burst out of the gates in its first year with four wins, including for lead actress in a drama (Tamara Tunie, winning her first-ever Emmy), emerging talent in a daytime drama series (for Ambyr Michelle), lighting direction and hairstyling/makeup.

	“This is the best ‘welcome back to daytime’ ever,” said Tunie, who first began working in the genre in 1987.

	“General Hospital’s” four wins, beside daytime drama, also included victories for for writing team and for guest performer in a daytime drama (Jeff Kober, who also earned a Primetime Emmy nomination this year for “The Pitt,” a rare double nomination for both awards shows in the same year).
	

	“Young and the Restless” won three, including supporting actor in a drama winner Roger Howarth (“The Young and the Restless”), who made Daytime Emmy history for the longest gap between wins (it’s been 32 years since he last won a Daytime Emmy). The show also won for supporting actress in a daytime drama (Beth Maitland). 

	In the first timers club, Star Jones won her first Daytime Emmy after 14 nominations — this time, in the daytime personality — daily category, for “Divorce Court.”

	The Daytime Emmys recognizes daytime dramas, talk series, entertainment news, culinary, adventure, instructional and legal/courtroom programming — and for the 53rd edition, that covers an eligibility calendar of Jan. 1, 2025 to Dec. 31, 2025. This year’s Daytime Emmys nominations come after serveral rule changes were announced this spring. 

	“General Hospital” icon Genie Francis was this year’s Lifetime Achievement honoree, presented by her husband, actor Jonathan Frakes. “The joy of doing the work has never left me,” she said. “I am so proud to be a member of the cast of ‘General Hospital.’ The caliber of this cast inspires me every day and keeps me humble.”

	Allen Media Group founder, chairman and CEO Byron Allen, host/executive producer Meredith Vieira,  performer Patrika Darbo and actor/director/executive producer Francesca James are this year’s Gold Circle inductees, while Fox Television Stations exec VP of programming and development Stephen Brown and announcer/warm-up host Rubin Ervin are Silver Circle inductees.

	There’s no host this year, but Matthew Hoffman served as announcer. Formerly held in June, the Daytime Emmys moved to mid-fall last year; the 2026 event took place as a single ceremony on Friday.

	CBS led all outlets with eight wins for the network (its syndication arm CBS Media Ventures won an additional two). The now-defunct NBCUniversal Syndication unit won five awards thanks to “Kelly Clarkson.”

	Here’s how the network/distribution tally went: CBS 8; NBCU Syndication  5; ABC 4; Inkblot 3

	And the series tally: “Kelly Clarkson” 5; “General Hospital” 4; “Beyond the Gates” 4; “Young and the Restless” 3; “A Different Breed” 3

title: Magical Realist Tale ‘6TM’ and ‘Searching for SmarterChild,’ About One of the Earliest Chatbots, Win Top Industry Awards at Ji.hlava Festival
description: “6TM,” directed by Karim Akalay and produced by Walid Bekhti, won the New Visions Award for the most promising European project at the Ji.hlava Doc
body:
“6TM,” directed by Karim Akalay and produced by Walid Bekhti, won the New Visions Award for the most promising European project at the Ji.hlava Documentary Film Festival on Friday. The film is described as “a Belgian family comedy in three chapters, rooted in magic realism and the resilience of a community.”

	In the film, which is set over one scorching summer in the Cité Modèle, Brussels’ largest housing project, three stories unfold across one family. Two kids chase a magic lamp to keep their wheelchair-using friend from being forced out by broken elevators. A teenage girl builds a team of misfits for a soccer tournament. A mother rallies her neighbors to uncover who stole the rain.
	

	The jury said, “With its imaginative blend of magical realism, humor and social relevance, ‘6TM ‘ offers a fresh vision of European cinema. Rooted in lived experience and shaped through co-creation, ‘6TM’ challenges conventional representations and opens up new possibilities for who gets to tell stories, whose voices are heard, and who sees themselves reflected on screen. We believe this approach holds extraordinary promise for the next generation of both audiences and filmmakers, demonstrating how cinema can become more inclusive and participatory.”

	The jury was composed of Katrine Kiilgaard, managing director of CPH:DOX in Denmark; Anda Ionescu, managing partner and producer at Tangaj Production in Romania; and Robert Y. Chang, co-producer of American Documentary at POV in the U.S.

	The award was presented in cooperation with UPP, which donated an in-kind grant for visual post-production worth about 15,000 Euros, and Soundaquare, which provided sound mixing and a final sound master, with an estimated value of 5,000 Euros.
	

	The New Visions Award for the most promising U.S. project went to “Searching for SmarterChild,” directed by Lindsey Sitz and Zan Gillies, and produced by Erin Williams-Weir.

	The U.S.-Canadian film looks back to 2003, and the creation of SmarterChild, an online chatbot. He became a sounding board for a generation. People confided in him, insulted him and propositioned him.

	Twenty years later, as AI becomes deeply embedded in our lives, what does our treatment of the first internet chatbot say about us? By revisiting our cringe-worthy conversations, the film explores the darkest parts of human nature, accountability, and what it takes to change, not only the technologies we create, but ourselves.

	The jury said, ” ‘Searching for SmarterChild’ takes us back to the early days of the internet to confront one of the most pressing questions of our time: what does our relationship with artificial intelligence reveal about ourselves? By revisiting their interactions with one of the earliest chatbots of their childhoods, the filmmakers offer a perspective on today’s fascination with AI, challenging us to reflect not only on the technologies we create, but also on how we treat them and each other. The jury wishes to recognize the project’s promise to engage audiences through an original, entertaining and thought-provoking approach to a subject that will profoundly shape our collective future.”

	The award was presented in partnership with AmDocs, with the winner receiving $7,000 in cash.

	The festival also accorded the APA World Excellence Award to renowned Danish producer Signe Byrge Sørensen. The award honors her “outstanding contribution to international film production and her remarkable achievements in world cinema.”

            Rep. Ilhan Omar reportedly crossed out her name -- not once but twice -- on her marriage application to Ahmed Nur Said Elmi.

            As you know, Omar has been facing longstanding allegations that she married Elmi to help him obtain legal immigration status.
      
    
            She previously told MS NOW's Chris Hayes that as far as she knows, Elmi is not her brother ... calling the allegations "insane."

description:
'SNL' Writer's Missing Sister
                          2 People Arrested on Suspicion of Murder
body:
'SNL' Writer's Missing Sister
                          2 People Arrested on Suspicion of Murder
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                October 30, 2026
                
                            3:27 PM PDT
                                                                      |

                                  October 30, 2026
                                6:21 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Two people have been arrested on suspicion of murder in connection with "Saturday Night Live" writer Jimmy Fowlie's sister's disappearance ... according to a report.
      
    
            NBC4 states authorities searched an Airbnb property in Joshua Tree earlier this month in connection with their search for Christina Lynn Downer ... working in conjunction with the San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department and using K-9 units.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            In April, Jimmy Fowlie stated his sister was "no longer alive" on Instagram ... though local authorities disputed the claim.
      

            LAPD told us at the time ... “Robbery-Homicide Division continues to investigate the disappearance of Christina Downer. Although the circumstances of her disappearance are suspicious, Ms. Downer has not been located, and her case has not been reclassified as a homicide. RHD will diligently investigate this case until a resolution can be reached.”
      
    
            We later learned Christina had a restraining order in 2024 against the ex-girlfriend of her then-boyfriend.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Christina was last seen in Los Angeles' Koreatown neighborhood in December 2025. Fowlie has said he believes his sister's social media was compromised in the weeks before her death.
      
    
            Anyone with information about Christina's case is asked to call the LAPD Missing Persons Unit at 213-996-1800. During non-business hours or on weekends, call 1-877-527-3247.
      
    
            We've reached out to law enforcement for more info ... so far, no word back.

title: Cheerleader Accused of Luring Boyfriend to Death Wants Bond Eased for Dorm Living
description:
Cheerleader Charged with Murder
                          I Want To Live In A College Dorm!!!
body:
Cheerleader Charged with Murder
                          I Want To Live In A College Dorm!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 30, 2026
                            6:07 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A cheerleader who allegedly orchestrated her boyfriend's murder is asking the court to ease up on her bond restrictions ... because she wants to have a normal college experience.
      
    
            According to ABC 15 News, 18-year-old Gianna Kistenmacher -- who's one of 9 people charged in the 2025 murder of her boyfriend, Trey Wright -- filed a motion last month, asking the court to toss her GPS monitoring and overnight curfew ... and allow her to access social media.
      
    
            Gianna is charged with murder in the 16-year-old's shooting death ... investigators allege she brought the shooter, Devan Raper, to Trey's house, knowing he was armed and there would be a fight.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            According to Court TV ... Trey and Devan had been arguing online about Devan hanging out with Gianna.
      
    
            The outlet reports 9 teenagers drove over to Trey's ... and when Trey came over to the car Devan was in, the 19-year-old shot him in the chest and killed him.
      
    
            Now, according to ABC 15 News, Gianna's motion notes that she's complied with all bond conditions since her release on July 28, 2025.
      
    
            She currently attends college locally -- a judge removed her house arrest in February and replaced it with an overnight curfew -- but wants the chance to apply to other schools and live in a dorm.
      
    
            Gianna's attorney has previously argued that she didn't orchestrate Trey's death ... and went to the hospital after the shooting to be with him.

title: Christa Pike Demands End to Solitary Confinement After Botched Execution
description:
Christa Pike
                          I Survived Death, Now I'm Suffering All Alone!!!
body:
Christa Pike
                          I Survived Death, Now I'm Suffering All Alone!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                October 30, 2026
                
                            2:03 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 30, 2026
                                3:46 PM PDT
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Christa Pike survived a botched execution ... but now she's fighting another battle behind bars, asking a federal judge to get her out of solitary confinement ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court documents, obtained by TMZ, Pike filed an emergency motion Friday, claiming Tennessee prison officials are violating a 2024 settlement agreement that was supposed to end her decades-long isolation.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Pike's attorneys say she's been kept alone in the prison infirmary since returning from the hospital Oct. 9 ... with officials refusing to say when she'll be allowed to interact with other inmates again.
      

            The docs say the settlement previously allowed Pike to work, eat meals, exercise, and socialize with other women in custody ... privileges her legal team says have now been stripped away.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Pike claims the isolation is taking a serious psychological toll ... especially after spending 28 years in solitary confinement before reaching the agreement ... saying in a sworn declaration each day she's kept alone only makes things worse.
      
    
            And she's raising concerns about her living conditions, too ... claiming she's been forced to clean a roach-infested shower herself, despite suffering severe burns, nerve damage, and painful wounds from the failed execution.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Her attorneys, Angie Bergman, Brian Roark and Hannah Webber, tell TMZ the state has ignored repeated warnings that Pike's isolation violates their agreement ... prompting them to seek emergency court intervention.
      
    
            Pike is asking to be housed alongside other women receiving medical care, where she says she could safely recover without being completely cut off from fellow inmates.
      
    
            She also requests the judge to fast-track the case ... proposing a Nov. 4 deadline for the state's response.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Pike survived Tennessee's Sept. 30 execution attempt despite receiving two doses of a lethal injection drug. She spent days on a ventilator and more than a week in intensive care.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The 50-year-old remains on death row for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer ... and Tennessee's governor has indicated he expects her death sentence will remain in place unless a court decides otherwise.
